title: Claim Status Voice Helpline for Policyholders
summary: An inbound voice agent that verifies callers, explains live claim status in plain language, sends pending-document lists on WhatsApp and transfers complaints and sensitive cases to people.

seo.title: Claim Status Voice Helpline with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: Multilingual voice agent that tells policyholders and hospitals where a claim stands, lists pending documents and routes complaints to your team.

problem.intro: 'Where is my claim?' is a question claims contact centres hear all day, from policyholders, family members and hospital insurance desks. Agents look up the claims system, decode internal status codes and read out pending documents, while callers with genuine complaints wait in the same queue.

pain_points.title: Status codes mean nothing to callers
pain_points.detail: Labels such as 'query raised' or 'under investigation' need explanation, and different agents explain them differently.

pain_points.title: Pending documents are hard to communicate
pain_points.detail: Deficiency letters list items in insurance language, so callers ring back after sending the wrong document.

pain_points.title: Peaks around discharge time
pain_points.detail: Calls spike when hospitals push for discharge approvals, and IVR menus cannot answer claim-specific questions.

pain_points.title: Complaints get buried
pain_points.detail: Callers unhappy with a deduction or rejection queue alongside simple status checks, and their complaint may not be logged properly.

solution.overview: We build an inbound voice agent for your claims helpline. It answers in the caller's language, verifies them against the registered mobile number and claim or policy details, and reads the live claim status from your claims or TPA system. Internal status codes are translated into plain explanations your team has approved. If documents are pending, it lists them simply and sends the deficiency letter and an upload link on WhatsApp. Settled claims get payment details after verification. Complaints, disputes about deductions and sensitive cases such as death claims go straight to a person with a call summary, and every interaction is logged as a ticket.
capabilities: Answers in Hindi, English and selected regional languages, detecting the caller's preference
Verifies callers using the registered mobile and claim or policy details before sharing anything
Reads live status from the claims or TPA system and explains it using approved templates
Lists pending documents in plain language and sends the deficiency letter and upload link on WhatsApp
Shares settlement amount, date and payment reference once the caller is verified
Transfers complaints, disputes and bereavement calls to a person and logs them in your grievance system

workflow.title: Answer and detect language
workflow.detail: The agent greets the caller, identifies the preferred language and asks for the claim or policy number.

workflow.title: Verify the caller
workflow.detail: Identity is checked against the registered mobile and policy details; unverified callers get general help only.

workflow.title: Fetch live status
workflow.detail: Claim stage, pending items and payment details are pulled from the claims or TPA system.

workflow.title: Explain and send documents
workflow.detail: Status is explained in plain language, and pending-document lists or letters are sent on WhatsApp.

workflow.title: Route complaints and sensitive cases
workflow.detail: Complaints, disputes and bereavement calls go to a claims executive with a summary.

workflow.title: Log the interaction
workflow.detail: A ticket with transcript, intent and outcome is created in the CRM or grievance system.

inputs: Live claim status and history from the claims or TPA system
Mapping of internal status codes to approved explanations
Settlement records with amount, date and payment reference
Registered mobile and policy details for verification
outputs: Plain-language status explanations delivered by voice
WhatsApp messages with deficiency letters and upload links
Complaint and grievance tickets with call summaries
Reports on top call reasons and confusing status codes
human_in_the_loop: Claims executives take every complaint, dispute and bereavement call, and the grievance team owns complaint resolution. Supervisors review samples of automated calls and approve any change to the status explanation templates.
integrations: CRM or ticketing such as Salesforce Service Cloud or Freshdesk
guardrails: Rejection and deduction reasons read only as recorded in the letter, with no speculation
No promises on settlement dates beyond what the system shows
Bereavement and distress detected early and handed to a person
Personal and health data redacted from transcripts and logs
compliance_notes: Every complaint is logged and routed into your grievance process, so the helpline supports the redressal mechanism IRDAI requires rather than bypassing it.
Health and identity data is shared only with verified callers, supporting DPDP Act 2023 obligations.

pilot.scope: Status queries on retail health reimbursement claims in Hindi and English during business hours, with fallback to your existing agents.
deliverables: Status code explanation library approved by claims and compliance
Working voice agent on a test line connected to claim status data

faqs.q: Can hospital insurance desks use it too?
faqs.a: Yes, with a separate verification path for hospitals, such as a provider ID and claim number. Hospital desks usually ask about cashless approval and enhancement status, which the agent reads from the same system.

faqs.q: Will it explain why a claim was rejected?
faqs.a: It reads the reason exactly as recorded in the rejection or deduction letter and offers to send the letter. If the caller disagrees, it registers a complaint and transfers them to a person rather than arguing the case.
A typical first phase covers Hindi and English, with regional languages added according to your policyholder base. We test each language on your own call recordings before go-live.
Verification happens before anything is shared, transcripts are redacted, and data stays in your chosen cloud region with role-based access.
